reran: cmd.sh: LimitExceededException 'Too many allocated bytes' on the integration build and on the base (about 8 s); 2.13.18 compiles the file in 2 min 8 s. A program I wrote by hand, one method with 220 consecutive lines of try { val r = k.f(i).map(x => x + i).filter(_ > 0).map(_ * 2).getOrElse(0); sb.append(...) } catch { case e: Throwable => sb.append(...) }, behaves the same with -opt:inline:** -opt:local: crash in 6 s on both local builds, compiles in 66 s on 2.13.18 and runs.
user_impact: Needs the inliner and one method with a couple of hundred try/catch blocks in sequence, each with some inlined closures. That is a test or main method that wraps each of many checks in try/catch, or generated code; not a typical application method, but a person can write it and code generators do. With 150 such lines the method compiles (17 s).
fixability: design question: the cause is the upgrade to ASM 9.11.1 (scala/scala#11327, Lukas Rytz, commit c8bc25a6d0), which is on 2.13.x after v2.13.19-M1. ASM 9.11 counts the bytes of every Frame it allocates during an analysis, garbage included, in an int; scalac lifts the limit to Int.MaxValue but cannot go higher. The failing method has 8153 instructions, 158 handlers and about 400 locals: the analysis revisits the tail of the method after each handler merge and allocates two handler frames per covered instruction per visit, so the count passes 2 GiB although live memory is small. Options: catch LimitExceededException in AsmAnalyzer users and skip the optimization for that method with an optimizer warning; add the handler count to the size estimate in AsmAnalyzer.sizeOK*, which today is instructions times locals squared and predicts under a second for this method; or widen or disable the counter in the scala-asm fork. The first is the smallest.
regression: in unreleased 2.13.19 (scala/scala#11327, ASM 9.11.1); not in v2.13.19-M1; not caused by a draft fix on the integration build
links: O1 is an unrelated ProdConsAnalyzer miscompile. None of the earlier findings concerns the ASM limits.
note: The finding's guess that the methods are far larger than hand-written code is wrong: the failing method is the harness's own Main.run, 8153 instructions after inlining, well under the JVM limit; what matters is the number of exception handlers. The commit message of the upgrade says the limits were lifted for scalac; they are only raised to the int maximum. 2.13.18's two minutes on the same file is the same quadratic analysis without a limit, so the size guard was already wrong for handler-heavy methods. The repro in the finding directory is still the 39 KB generated file; the hand-written generator is a ten-line shell loop described under reran, and was left in the review scratch directory (ge6/H220.scala). No report found in scala/bug, scala/scala or scala/scala-asm.
